test_title: PYST 25: SSC GD Constable 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 17 Feb, 2025 - Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: In what reference was ‘Growth’ the goal of all the five-year plans?

options.text: Growth of country’s capacity to produce goods and services
Growth in foreign investment in the country
Growth in the import of goods and services in the country

solution:
The correct answer is __**Growth of country's capacity to produce goods and services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "growth" in the context of the five-year plans refers to the **country's capacity to produce goods and services**, measured by economic indicators like Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• All five-year plans aimed at ensuring **self-reliance, modernization, and economic development** through industrialization, agricultural growth, and infrastructure development.
 
• The primary goal of the plans was to achieve a sustained increase in production capacity to meet the needs of the growing population and reduce reliance on imports.
 
• Economic growth was seen as the cornerstone for improving living standards, reducing poverty, and achieving balanced regional development.
 
• For example, the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61) emphasized **rapid industrialization** and the growth of capital goods industries to strengthen the economic base of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP):** GDP is the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period, serving as a primary indicator of economic growth.
 
• **Planned Economy:** India adopted a planned economic model post-independence, where the government played a central role in setting production targets and resource allocation through five-year plans.
 
• **Self-Reliance:** A key objective was to reduce dependence on foreign aid and imports by developing indigenous industries and enhancing production capacity.
 
• **Balanced Regional Development:** Special focus was placed on reducing regional disparities by encouraging growth in backward and underdeveloped areas.
 
• **Role of the Planning Commission:** The Planning Commission (now replaced by NITI Aayog) was responsible for formulating and overseeing the implementation of five-year plans to achieve economic growth and social welfare objectives.
